title: fix(sse): streaming chunking & framing fixes for partial JSON, delimiter ordering and token-event ordering
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Context: We observed multiple customer reports and internal canary failures where SSE responses could emit partial JSON payloads across chunk boundaries, as well as occasional delimiter ordering regressions after the OpenAI-compat streaming bridge refactor. Root causes: (1) the SSE framing code did not consistently prefer event-boundary delimiters when flushing buffers, leading to 'partial JSON' chunks being emitted; (2) the token->event conversion path could reorder delimiter events when a multi-token JSON structure crossed internal batching boundaries; (3) the compatibility layer for OpenAI streaming occasionally injected an extra '\n' delimiter when a tool-call event followed a text chunk. This PR fixes the framing and ordering problems, adds unit and integration tests, and includes a small refactor to make flush points explicit.

What this change does:
- Fixes framing: the SSE emitter now tracks event boundaries and prefers to flush on full-event delimiters rather than arbitrary token boundaries. This prevents partial JSON objects being split across chunks.
- Fixes delimiter ordering: token->event pipeline updated to preserve explicit delimiter events and ensure tool/function-calling events are emitted before trailing text delimiters when required by the OpenAI streaming compatibility contract.
- Adds a small API: sse.Emitter.FlushAtEventBoundary() used by the bridge and runtime to indicate safe flush points.
- Adds tests: expanded unit tests covering partial JSON sequences and a new e2e integration test that simulates a tool-calling sequence crossing batching boundaries.
- Docs: documents the expected ordering guarantees in docs/api/streaming.md and adds a note for SDKs.

Checklist:
- [x] Reproduced failing sequences locally and in canary
- [x] Added unit/integration tests
- [x] Updated docs
- [x] Added changelog/release notes

Risk/rollout: Low risk; change is limited to SSE framing and the OpenAI-compat bridge. Backwards compatible for consumers, but fixes ordering that may alter the boundary of chunks (should only improve client parsing). Will watch canary for increased error counts during rollout.

review_comments: Diego Martinez (2026-02-16): Can you add a comment explaining why we choose event-boundary flushing vs max-chunk-size? I worry about memory for very long events.
Aisha Patel (2026-02-16): Good point — added a comment and a configurable safety cap; default unchanged. Long events are guarded by the existing max-chunk-size.
Meera Singh (2026-02-18): The integration test is flaky on my run — can we make the timing deterministic by stubbing the batcher?
Aisha Patel (2026-02-19): Updated the test to inject a deterministic batcher; reran locally and on CI.
Evan Liu (2026-02-24): Approved after the tests and minor naming nits are addressed.
release_notes: Fix SSE streaming chunking and framing to avoid partial JSON emissions and ensure correct delimiter/event ordering for OpenAI-compatible streaming. Users should see improved streaming stability and fewer partial-JSON parse errors in clients.
